### Observed differences

- Three activities that were absent or nearly absent in the earlier window occur regularly in the later window: A19 in about 38 in 100 traces (0 of 200 earlier), A25 in about 35 in 100 (0 earlier) and A20 in about 30 in 100 (1 of 200 earlier), in each case at most once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- Routing out of A41 changed fundamentally. Earlier, about 82 in 100 of A41's observed outgoing transitions went directly to A26; in the later window only about 1–2 in 100 do, while about 87 in 100 go to one of the three activities above — A19 (~33), A25 (~30) or A20 (~24). [DIR004]
- The new activities sit between A41 and A26. In the later window, essentially every trace containing one of them also contains A41 before it and A26 after it (about 75 of the 76 traces with A19, 65–66 of 69 with A25, 56–57 of 59 with A20), and A19's and A25's own outgoing transitions lead to A26 in about 95 and 90 in 100 cases respectively. All three appear at a similar relative position, roughly a third of the way through the trace. Earlier, A26 was present in every trace while A19 and A25 never occurred and A20 almost never. [REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- The three new activities behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: any two of them co-occur in only about 0.5–1.5 in 100 traces, while typically exactly one of them appears (A19 alone about 37 in 100, A25 alone about 33, A20 alone about 29). [REL001, REL002, REL005]
- A26 itself is unchanged in participation — present in every trace in both windows — but its relative event position moved slightly later (mean about 0.37 to about 0.40), consistent with activities now executing before it. [POS004]
- A secondary difference: among A02's observed outgoing transitions, A26 fell from about 26 in 100 earlier to not observed later; this rests on few transitions (35 earlier, 44 later). [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, a mutually exclusive choice among three activities — A19, A20 and A25 — was inserted on the path between A41 and A26. Earlier, A41 led directly to A26 in about 82 of 100 of its observed outgoing transitions and A19/A25 were not observed at all; in the later window the direct A41→A26 step accounts for only about 1–2 in 100 of A41's outgoing transitions, A41 instead leads to A19, A25 or A20 (about 87 in 100 combined), and each of the three — now present in roughly 30–38% of traces — is preceded by A41 and followed by A26 in nearly every trace in which it occurs, with the three rarely occurring together. A26 remains mandatory and its slightly later relative position fits this pattern. The screening qualified 20 control-flow items where about 0.51 would be expected without a change — roughly 40 times the chance expectation — and each item's difference exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits; the relational and successor evidence shows the new ordering directly rather than relying on frequency shifts alone. [DIR004, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL005, POS004]

The evidence cannot rule out that A19, A20 and A25 already existed in the earlier process at rates too low to appear in 200 traces — zero participation only means "not observed" — in which case the change would be an extreme shift in the use of an existing path rather than a genuinely new fragment. The items also largely describe one underlying trace behaviour, so they corroborate one another but are not independent confirmations. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]

Other differences: A02's successor mix changed — A26 is no longer observed among A02's outgoing transitions (about 26 in 100 earlier, on 35 versus 44 transitions) — but the evidence does not link this to the A41–A26 path. [DIR001]
